## Purpose

Operator-run, one-off maintenance scripts — data migration, forensic audit, build-time asset
generation, and test-environment seeding. Each is invoked manually
(`python scripts/<name>.py`); **none is imported by the application or run automatically**.

## Shape

- [backend/scripts/audit_lost_run_events.py](../../backend/scripts/audit_lost_run_events.py) — strictly read-only forensic audit (opens
  SQLite with a `mode=ro` URI, issues only SELECTs) that re-simulates the pre-FIX-240 seq
  allocator to name which `run_events` rows a historical seq-collision destroyed. Reports
  `WALKED-ONTO` losses and `ORPHAN-CARD` tombstones; explicitly refuses to ever become a
  repair path, because a back-filled row would mint an `event_id` the engine never emitted.

- [backend/scripts/cutover_legacy_runs.py](../../backend/scripts/cutover_legacy_runs.py) — one-time deployment-window script (T021b) that
  cancels any non-terminal `WorkflowRun` created by the pre-Universal-Execution-Engine legacy
  runners (identified by a missing `pipeline_run_id`), run once before deleting those legacy
  runner files. Supports `--dry-run`.

- [backend/scripts/generate_template_thumbnails.py](../../backend/scripts/generate_template_thumbnails.py) — build-time step that screenshots each
  `design-templates/<id>/example.html` via headless Chromium (Playwright) at 1280x720 and
  writes `thumbnail.jpg`, baked into the backend Docker image build. Best-effort by design
  (always exits 0); templates without a thumbnail fall back to a live `<iframe>` in the
  catalog UI.

- [backend/scripts/seed_test_users.py](../../backend/scripts/seed_test_users.py) — idempotently upserts one QA user per tier
  (`basic`/`pro`/`enterprise`/`enterprise`+admin) via direct DB insert and the app's own
  password hasher, for the live Playwright E2E suite (login is otherwise unreachable since
  registration is disabled and user creation is admin-only).

## Why this shape

These are deliberately kept as standalone scripts rather than app-layer endpoints or
management commands: each does something an admin does rarely and consciously — repair a
stuck deployment, prove a historical data loss, warm a build artifact, or bootstrap test
fixtures — and **none should be reachable over HTTP or triggered by a request**.

Several import directly from `app.models`/`agents.execution_engine` by inserting `backend/`
onto `sys.path`, since they run outside the FastAPI app context. The audit script enforces
its read-only contract at the connection level (SQLite `mode=ro`) **rather than by convention
alone**.

Not included here: anything that runs on a schedule or as part of CI — these are all
human-triggered, and the module holds no shared library code of its own beyond what each
script needs.
